text:
matt.garcia: quick Q — setting up AWS KMS for Redwood Private (VPC) control-plane + data-plane encryption. Need a clear onboarding checklist for customers: CMK choices, grants vs IAM role, DEK caching TTLs, rewrap strategy. Any blockers?

sara.chen: TL;DR: customer-owned CMK as KEK, GenerateDataKey for DEKs, cache unwrapped DEKs in-memory with TTL, ReEncrypt for rotation. Avoid KMS calls on hot-path.

olivia.khan: prefer grants for intra-account short-lived access. Grants cut down DescribeKey/calls and let us revoke quickly if needed. CreateGrant on bootstrap, store grantId for revoke.

deploy-bot: perf-check: load test started — 2k GenerateDataKey calls over 60s

sara.chen: sample key policy we request from customers (replace ARNs):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane" },
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:Encrypt"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

sara.chen: runtime role perms should be scoped to the CMK ARNs and include: GenerateDataKey, Decrypt, ReEncrypt*, DescribeKey, CreateGrant, ListGrants, RevokeGrant. ListKeys only for admin ops.

matt.garcia: DEK caching — recommended TTL? we want low latency but manageable rewrap.

olivia.khan: start with 5–15m TTL. Use cache key = <cmk-id>:<dek-version>:<tenant-id>. Invalidate on rewrap or when grant revoked. Zeroize plaintext on eviction.

devops-bot: perf-note: observed p95 GenerateDataKey ~40ms with regional KMS + retries

sara.chen: rotation flow we recommend:
1) Customer creates new CMK (or rotates key material) and updates KEK pointer.
2) Control-plane uses new CMK for new DEKs.
3) Background job ReEncrypts existing DEK ciphertexts to the new KEK in small batches.
4) After successful rewrap, bump DEK version and invalidate caches.

olivia.khan: aws cli example for rewrap:

```
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.cipher --source-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/old --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/new
```

sara.chen: for large numbers of DEKs do batched workers with exponential backoff on ThrottlingException. Track progress in migration table until completion.

sec-oncall: incident playbook if KEK compromised:
- Disable CMK immediately.
- Revoke grants (store grantIds at creation so you can revoke programmatically).
- Provision emergency KEK, update KEK pointer.
- Start bulk ReEncrypt to emergency KEK.
- Notify compliance/legal and rotate any affected credentials.

matt.garcia: do we ever store plaintext DEKs on disk?

olivia.khan: never. plaintext DEKs only in secure in-memory caches on control-plane hosts. Data-plane workers only hold ciphertext DEKs and call KMS/unwrap at startup if allowed.

sara.chen: telemetry we need in Redwood Console for Private:
- KMS call counts per tenant (GenerateDataKey, Decrypt, ReEncrypt)
- DEK cache hit ratio
- Failed Decrypt rate and error types
- Rewrap migration progress and throughput

matt.garcia: thresholds/alerts?

sara.chen: alert if Decrypt failure rate >0.5% over 5m or if cache-hit < 70% sustained during peak. Auto-fallback: if Decrypt spikes, temporarily serve from stale cache and page sec-oncall.

olivia.khan: BYOK/on-prem notes: CloudHSM-backed CMKs have quotas and often higher latency. Coordinate rewrap windows with customer to avoid throttling.

matt.garcia: got it. I'll draft the onboarding checklist (policy snippet, IAM role, grant guidance, rewrap plan, alert thresholds) and share. Thanks :thumbsup:
